subject: System Design
title: Serverless Computing
description: A fast breakdown of Serverless Computing for builders.

hook.text: You write a function. It runs when a request arrives. You pay only for the milliseconds it executes.

buildup.text: Serverless platforms like AWS Lambda and Cloudflare Workers manage all infrastructure automatically.

discovery.text: No provisioning, no patching, no scaling decisions. The platform handles everything from zero to millions.

twist.text: Cold starts add latency. The first request after idle time takes 100-500ms while the function boots up.

climax.text: Serverless is ideal for event-driven, bursty workloads. It's costly for steady, high-throughput traffic.

punchline.text: No servers to manage — pay per millisecond of execution.

quiz.question: What is a cold start in serverless computing?
options: Extra latency when a function boots up after being idle
The initial deployment of a function
